title: Terraform introduces tfpolicy support for Stacks, SCIM support, and more
content:
Over the past quarter, the HashiCorp Terraform engineering team has introduced new capabilities that make infrastructure management more scalable, secure, and easier to automate. These updates help platform teams streamline large-scale deployments, simplify operations with AI-ready workflows, strengthen security and governance, and manage infrastructure more efficiently. The latest HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise improvements include: 

  • Terraform policy support for Stacks 

  • Multi-deployment group orchestration 

  • Agent-ready Terraform Stacks CLI 

  • SCIM user lifecycle management 

Terraform Policy Support for Stacks 

Feature gap: As organizations adopt Terraform Stacks to manage infrastructure at scale, platform teams need the same governance guardrails they rely on for standard workspaces. Extending Terraform policy, HashiCorp's native, HCL-based policy-as-code framework, to Stacks gives teams a consistent way to enforce compliance and security standards as they scale multi-account and multi-region deployments. 

What's new: We are excited to introduce the general availability (GA) of Terraform policy support for Stacks, available for HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise. Platform teams can now apply HCL-based policies against Stacks, extending governance across infrastructure deployments. 

HCP Terraform runs policy evaluations after each deployment plan completes and re-evaluates policies for every subsequent plan-and-apply cycle when deployments have deferred changes. Platform teams can scope Terraform policy sets to all Stacks and workspaces in an organization, to specific projects, or to individual Stacks, giving them the same fine-grained control they have with workspaces today.   

Benefits: 

• Consistent governance across Stacks and workspaces: Platform teams can enforce the same HCL-based policies across Stacks and standard workspaces, so security and compliance guardrails apply everywhere infrastructure is provisioned. 

• Early feedback in the deployment lifecycle: Because policies evaluate immediately after each deployment's plan, teams catch policy violations before changes are applied, reducing the risk of non-compliant infrastructure reaching production. 

• Familiar authoring experience: Since Terraform policy uses HCL, the same language as Terraform, practitioners can write, test, and version-control Stacks policies using workflows they already know. 

To learn more, check out the Policy enforcement for Stacks documentation. 

Multi-Deployment Group Orchestration 

Feature gap: As Terraform Stacks scales to support hundreds of deployments, platform teams need a safe and efficient way to coordinate rollouts across large infrastructure fleets. Prior to this enhancement, Custom Deployment Groups were limited to a one-to-one relationship with deployments, providing organizational structure but lacking the orchestration controls needed to manage rollout risk, concurrency, and visibility at scale. 

What's new: We are introducing the general availability of multi-deployment group orchestration for HCP Terraform Premium and Terraform Enterprise. Deployment groups now evolve into true orchestration primitives capable of coordinating multiple deployments as a single rollout unit. Teams can define a failure tolerance threshold to automatically limit rollout blast radius, use eager planning controls to delay large-scale plan generation until explicitly triggered, and monitor rollout progress through new group-level visibility and management experiences. Together, these capabilities allow customers to safely scale deployment operations from tens to hundreds of deployments while maintaining control and observability. 

Benefits: 

  • Safer large-scale rollouts: Failure tolerance automatically throttles rollout progression and, once the configured threshold is exceeded, stops applying additional deployments in the group, reducing the risk of widespread production impact. 

  • Improved operational efficiency: Eager planning controls help avoid excessive plan generation, API rate limiting, and resource contention in large environments. 

  • Centralized rollout management: Platform engineers can manage groups of deployments as a single unit, using aggregated status views and group-level actions to simplify operations. 

  • Enhanced visibility: Dedicated Deployment group views provide a consolidated picture of rollout health, including success, failure, and blocked deployment counts, making it easier to diagnose and recover from issues. 

To learn more, check out deployment runs documentation. 

Agent-Ready Terraform Stacks CLI 

Feature gap: As organizations increasingly adopt AI-assisted operations, platform teams need infrastructure workflows that can be executed, monitored, and debugged programmatically. Terraform Stacks has continued expanding its CLI experience to support these emerging automation patterns, making it easier for users and AI agents to operate Stacks within CI/CD pipelines and other headless environments. 

What's new: We are introducing the general availability of a significant expansion of the Terraform Stacks CLI focused on agent-ready workflows. New non-interactive commands enable deployment monitoring, diagnostics, deployment and configuration inspection, and artifact access directly from the CLI. New monitoring commands such as terraform stacks deployment-run watch and terraform stacks deployment-group watch provide real-time visibility into deployment execution directly from the CLI. We also introduced broader JSON output support, allowing commands to return structured, machine-readable results that integrate seamlessly with AI agents and automation tooling. These enhancements make it easier for users to monitor deployments, investigate failures, and interact with Terraform Stacks through a consistent CLI experience without relying on custom API integrations.  

Benefits: 

  • Built for AI agents and automation: Non-interactive commands and structured JSON responses make it easier for AI agents, CI/CD systems, and other automated workflows to operate Terraform Stacks programmatically. 

  • Enhanced deployment visibility: New CLI commands provide direct access to deployment, configuration, and deployment-step information, simplifying deployment monitoring and status investigation. 

  • Accelerated troubleshooting: Expanded diagnostics capabilities help engineers quickly identify and understand configuration preparation issues, deployment failures, and step-level errors. 

  • Simplified integrations: Structured JSON output support provides predictable, machine-readable outputs that can be consumed by automation platforms without custom API tooling. 

  • Improved developer experience: Common operational tasks such as monitoring deployment progress, inspecting deployment artifacts, and diagnosing failures are now accessible through intuitive CLI commands, reducing workflow complexity and improving productivity. 

To learn more, check out the Stacks CLI documentation. 

SCIM User Lifecycle Management 

Feature gap: Enterprise organizations rely on their identity provider as the source of truth for user provisioning and deprovisioning. With SAML SSO alone, removing a user from the IdP doesn't remove their access to HCP Terraform and active sessions and API tokens can persist, creating security risk and compliance gaps. Manually managing users and team memberships can be error-prone and slow. 

What's new: We are excited to announce the general availability of System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) 2.0 support for HCP Terraform Standard and Premium customers. This integration enables automated user lifecycle management through integration with enterprise identity providers, improving security and compliance by automating user provisioning, de-provisioning, and team membership synchronization.  

When a user is deprovisioned in your identity provider, their access is automatically revoked, including active sessions and API tokens. New users are created automatically and added to the right teams based on membership of groups in your identity provider. Team memberships stay in sync, ensuring access control aligns with your identity provider as the source of truth without manual intervention. 

Benefits: 

  • No manual account management: Team memberships are continuously synchronized. New users are created and added to the appropriate teams based on group membership. Access is revoked when a user is removed from your identity provider, including active sessions and API tokens. 

  • Faster onboarding: SCIM-provisioned accounts skip email verification, so new team members get access immediately. 

  • Audit-ready compliance: All SCIM-initiated actions are logged in your organization's audit trail. This gives security and compliance reviews complete visibility. 

To learn more, check out the SCIM provisioning documentation.
